106:

**without process of fermentation**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 74d}}:—of bread, **unleavened**, ἄρτος{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 3.79, 1st c.BC: Trypho Grammaticus “Fragmenta” 117}}; ἄρτους ἀ., ἄζυμα λάγανα, {{LXX|LXX.Exo.29.2, LXX.Lev.2.4: _absolutely_, ἄζυμα, τά, LXX.Exo.12.15; τὰ ἄ.}}**the feast of unleavened cakes,** {{NT|NT.Mark.14.1}}; ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν ἀ. {{LXX+NT|LXX.2Ch.8.13, +others, NT.Luke.22.1.}}

120:
** ἀθῡμ-έω**,
**to be disheartened, despond**, ἐς νόσον πεσὼν ἀθυμεῖς{{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 474; οἴμ᾽ ὡς ἀθυμῶ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 587}}; ἀ τινι. **at** or **for** a thing, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. author] “El.” 769, etc.; ἐπί τινι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.3; εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 264b; πρὸς τὴν παροῦσαν ὄψιν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.88; τὴν τελευτήν [prev. author] 5.91; τοῦτο, ὡς.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 8.21; ἕνεκά τινος [prev. author] “An.” 5.4.19}}:—**to be sore afraid** lest, ἀθυμῶ δ᾽ εἰ φανήσομαι{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 666; δεινῶς ἀθυμῶ μὴ βλέπων ὁ μάντις ᾖ [prev. author] “OT” 747.}}
122:
** αἴγειος**, α, ον,
**of a goat**, αἴγειον κνῆ τυρόν {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.639, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ γυναικείης φύσιος” 38}}; ἀσκῷ ἐν αἰγείῳ in a **goat's** skin, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3. 247}}; αἰγείη κυνέη a helmet **of goatskin**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.231}}; γάλα αἴ. {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 522a23}}; κρέα αἴ. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus (Sp._) 49.}}
123:
** αἰγιᾰλός**, ὁ,
**sea-shore, beach**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.422, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.385, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.50, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.7 (_plural_), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.4, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 7.13.8 (_plural_), etc.}}; distinguished from ἀκτή, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 547a10; also in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus (Lyric poetry), “IT” 425, “IA” 210}}; αἰγιαλὸν ἔνδον τρέφει **a whole beach of voting-pelbles**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 110: proverbial, αἰγιαλῷ λαλεῖς}}, of deaf persons, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus, 2nd c.AD: Zenobius Paroemiographus 1.38. (Prob. connected with αἰγίς II, αἴξ IV.)}}
126:
** ἀΐδιος** [ᾱῐδ], ον,
also η, ον, {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Hymni” 10.21, +others}}, (ἀεί):— **everlasting, eternal,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|Hymni Homerici 29.3, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 310; frequently in Prose, χρόνος 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.21; ἔχθρα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.20}}; οἴκησις, of a tomb, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 11.16}}; ἡ ἀ. οὐσία **eternity**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 37e}}; ἀ. στρατηγία, ἀρχή, βασιλεία, **perpetual**.., {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1285a7, 1317b41, 1301b27; ἀ. βασιλεῖς, γέροντες, [prev. work] 1284b33, 1306a17}}; τὰ ἀ., opposed to τὰ γενητά and φθαρτά, {{Refs|[prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1069a32, “EN” 1139b23, +others}}; ἐς ἀΐδιον **for ever**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.63}}; **ad infinitum**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 640a6; ἐξ ἀϊδίου 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.1.3}}: _comparative_ **-ώτερος**{{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 284a17:}} —ἀ. is distinct from αἰώνιος as **everlasting** from **timeless**, {{Refs 6th c.AD+|6th c.AD: Olympiodorus Philosophus “in Aristotelis Meteora commentaria - pars” 146.16}}; but distinct from ἀείζωος as **eternal** (without beginning or end) from **everliving,** {{Refs|Corp.Herm. 8.2}}. _adverb_ **-ίως**{{LXX+2nd c.AD+|2nd-3rd c.AD: Symmachus LXX.Mic.7.18, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de communi mathematica scientia” 1, 5th c.AD: Hierocles Platonicus Philosophus “in Carmen Aureum - FPG” 1p.419M.}}
